title: The Question of Authority
text:
Literary criticism has long debated whether a text possesses a fixed meaning or whether meaning is produced anew by each reader. Structuralists sought to uncover the underlying systems that govern narrative, while reader-response theorists argued that the act of interpretation is inseparable from the reader's own experience. Such disagreements are not merely academic; they determine how a canonical work is taught and valued. Consequently, the question of authority has become central to the discipline.

Critics who reject the notion of an authoritative reading often invoke the ambiguity inherent in language itself. Yet this relativism has been criticised for dissolving the distinction between a careful interpretation and a careless one. A more nuanced position holds that texts constrain the range of plausible readings without dictating a single correct one. Such a view preserves both the stability of the work and the plurality of its interpreters.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what did structuralists try to uncover?
options: The underlying systems that govern narrative
The historical accuracy of the setting

questions.text: What has the relativist position been criticised for?
options: Ignoring the historical period of the text
Dissolving the distinction between careful and careless interpretation

questions.text: What does the nuanced position imply about texts?
options: They permit no interpretation at all
They limit the range of interpretations without fixing one reading
They have no effect on their readers
They can be read in any way without consequence

questions.text: Why does the passage describe the question of authority as central to the discipline?
options: Because it shapes how canonical works are taught and valued
Because scholars have already reached a firm consensus on it
Because it concerns only publishers and booksellers
Because authors never agree on the meaning of their own work

paragraph_translations: A crítica literária há muito debate se um texto possui um significado fixo ou se o sentido é produzido de novo por cada leitor. Os estruturalistas buscavam revelar os sistemas subjacentes que regem a narrativa, enquanto os teóricos da recepção argumentavam que o ato de interpretar é inseparável da experiência do próprio leitor. Essas divergências não são meramente acadêmicas; elas determinam como uma obra canônica é ensinada e valorizada. Consequentemente, a questão da autoridade tornou-se central para a disciplina.

Críticos que rejeitam a noção de uma leitura autorizada frequentemente invocam a ambiguidade inerente à própria linguagem. No entanto, esse relativismo tem sido criticado por dissolver a distinção entre uma interpretação cuidadosa e uma descuidada. Uma posição mais matizada sustenta que os textos restringem o leque de leituras plausíveis sem ditar uma única leitura correta. Tal visão preserva tanto a estabilidade da obra quanto a pluralidade de seus intérpretes.
